reference.title: Wi-Fi Configuration view -
reference.shortdesc: The Wi-Fi Configuration view is the primary view for configuring Wi-Fi communications on both the and the controllers. The view includes tabs for configuring the controller to run in both Client mode and Access Point mode. However, a controller unit cannot perform in both modes at the same time.

section.p: The topics that follow provide additional details about the Wi-Fi Configuration view in : PlatformViewsWi-Fi Configuration.

The information in this view is organized in three major groups: Host Configuration, Client Mode tab, Access Point Mode tab. Values are shown in each view but are editable only when appropriate, based on the current active Wi-Fi state (Enabled: true or false) and mode (Switch Position), as selected and shown in the Host Configuration group properties.

section.title: Host Configuration properties
section.p: The Host Configuration property group is located at the top of the Wi-Fi Configuration view. These properties are described in the following table.

property.propdesc: The true option enables Wi-Fi and the false option disables Wi-Fi on the connected controller. Any change in this value requires a reboot to implement.

property.propvalue: Off, Client, Access Point, Access Point Controlled

propdesc.note: There is no physical "switch" on the .

ul.li: Off sets controller Wi-Fi operation off.
Client sets controller Wi-Fi to function in Client mode.
Access Point sets Wi-Fi to function in Access Point mode.

Access Point Controlled sets controller Wi-Fi to function as an access point using the same properties as the Access Point option but with the added ability to act in response to the controller Wi-Fi button presses. See for more details.

This is the result of toggling the Wi-Fi Enabled control from true to false in the platform's Wi-Fi Configuration view, or an access point Inactivity Timeout occurred. In the case of an inactivity timeout, the next state will be Inactivity Timeout after which the Wi-Fi connection stops.
In all other cases, the next state will be Stopped.

section.title: Client Mode Wi-Fi states
section.p: The following current Wi-Fi states are specific to Client mode.

property.propvalue: Indicates that Client mode is running but not active.
property.propdesc: This status displays when Client mode is inactive and not connected to an Access Point.

property.propvalue: Reports that the adapter is up and the IP assigned.
property.propdesc: Client successfully established the connection with Access Point.

property.propvalue: Indicates that the Client mode Wi-Fi adapter is looking for an access point to connect to by scanning available frequencies.
property.propdesc: This can happen if the Wi-Fi network (ssid/password, etc) is not configured correctly or is unavailable because the access point is off or out of range.

property.propvalue: Indicates that a configured access point has been located, and the supplicant is trying to associate with the access point.
property.propdesc: If the Allow List is configured in the access point, the mac address of this client adapter must pass the list filters.

property.propvalue: Indicates that the Client mode supplicant is negotiating capabilities and credentials with the access point.
property.propdesc: If successful, the next transition will be to Client Running.

property.propvalue: Indicates that the Client has successfully associated with an access point.
property.propdesc: The Client and access point begin a four-way handshake to validate credentials and establish common security protocol suites (see "Client Negotiating").

property.propvalue: Reports a normal state transition on Client mode startup.
property.propdesc: It is normal to see this during Client mode startup, but should transition to other states. If no configured access points are available, the connection does not progress past this point. Every 15 seconds, the network database is reloaded, so that configuration changes made during this state are picked up.

property.propvalue: Indicates tha the Client mode is not currently capable of running.
property.propdesc: This state displays when a client process encounters a faulty or unknown state. This state may also result from configuration errors or a failure in the CC and SKU validation process.

section.title: Access Point mode Wi-Fi states
section.p: The following current Wi-Fi states are specific to Access Point mode.

property.propvalue: Reports that the Access Point mode is enabled in the Wi-Fi Configuration view.
property.propdesc: This starts the Wi-Fi driver, which adds a wlan0 adapter, brings the adapter up and assigns an IP address to it, starts Hostapd, and starts the Dhcp server on the adapter. This state can only be entered from the Stopped state.

property.propvalue: Reports that the adapter is up and the IP address assigned.
property.propdesc: The Hostapd started and the Dhcp server started on the adapter.

property.propvalue: In Access Point Controlled mode, a non-zero Inactivity Timeout value is used to provide Access Mode capability. If, for the specified amount of time, no clients are connected or attached, the adapter is shut down in this state.
property.propdesc:
Inactivity timeout is only used in Access Point Controlled mode.ActiveAn Access Point is considered "Active" if at least one client is connected, regardless of whether or not there are any current non-broadcast communications.InactiveAn Access Point is considered "Inactive" if no clients are connected for the specified Inactivity Timeout value.
To restart the Wi-Fi adapter after an Inactivity Timeout shutdown, you must press the Wi-Fi button on the controller. Timed access restarts using the current Inactivity Timeout setting.

property.propvalue: Reports that there is a fault, unknown state or configuration error.
property.propdesc: This state indicates that the service is not started because Wi-Fi properties are not correctly configured, service is not enabled or in some other fault state.
